findings.claim: Planted claim is FALSE. cost_above loops `for back in 1..=2`, so it checks both lines above the fence and skips blank ones with `continue`. A cost line two lines up, with a blank line between, is therefore found and reported as its class, not `trivial`. The unit test `looks_back_two_lines_to_the_last_non_blank` (line 321) decides it: line 324 asserts that `<!-- example-cost: gpu -->\n \t\n```rust` contains `"gpu"`. Line 325 shows that two blank lines in between give `trivial`. The parity fixture `ebe_lookback` covers the same case against the .py.
